they are functionally the same

i actually think few years from now launching coins will be completely derisked

issue is everytime you do something you deplete your social capital

for instance most celeb coins last cycle were scams in that the supply was bought by insiders and dumped shortly after launch onto retail’s heads using said celeb’s social media posts as an attention funnel, celebs took payment and then never talked about the coins again - the possible difference here will be how they decide to launch the coin & how they decide to talk about it afterwards

boner is a meme attached to the stock hims, it also has a dev team and ppl who were insiders to that team bought early, like any other memecoin its value will be determined by how much attention it can continue to generate, which will be driven by the community talking about it and possibly catalysts attached to ppl associated with the stock hims

i have no insight into @HunterBiden’s teams plans or what their intents are, only that every other person external to crypto (incl. trump) who decided to launch a coin decided not to mention it again ever after the first week or so except maybe iggy, & they historically have 99.9% been “scams” 

but you are correct in that they are functionally the same, difference is when the attention on each coin peaks, for some community driven coins the attention peaks later, for the celeb coins the attention usually peaks in the first block

3. cut losses really quick and never hold onto the idea that the coins will rebound back to breakeven

The fees and slippages are criminal though.
